text: How many men should I have on my roster? How many men do you recommend talking to? As many as you can, as you can do. I don't know your guys' schedule. If you want to be married in 2025, then you need to get on a game plan to where you're going on multiple dates per week. Dating one man at a time and then waiting and hoping and praying that he's going to propose to you is not going to work. When I got proposed to, my roster was still texting me days after that. Up until the day I was proposed to, options were still optioning. Look, I can understand when a woman goes on multiple dates while she's single. Fair game. But when she's already dating someone and still going on other dates behind her man's back, sleeping with other guys, or running a whole roster to increase her chances of getting married, that is evil. There is no cute spin for that. And what makes it worse is how casually she talks about it, like it's something she's proud of. Relationship isn't a game where you try to maximize your options while someone else is investing real feelings, time, and effort into you. If you don't want to be committed, say it. If you want to explore, say it. Be single and do what you want. But deceiving someone who thinks you're building something together, that is cruel. And here's the part nobody wants to say out loud. Women like this burn good men. Guys who genuinely try, who show up, who treat their partner well. They get betrayed and humiliated, and then they swear off dating, thinking every woman is like that. And ironically, women who actually want a real relationship pay the price. So guys, listen carefully. If a woman tells you she's keeping her options open while expecting you to treat her like a boyfriend, walk away. If she brags about playing men against each other, walk away. If she thinks commitment is optional until she is ready to settle down, walk away. There are women who value loyalty, honesty, and stability. Focus on them. Don't waste a single second trying to win someone who treats relationships like a competition.
